neighbours.label: Words in a passage about passing property or money on to heirs at death (inheritance, wills, estates); fires on function words and verbs such as when/leave/among/your there, not on 'after' or 'leave' in everyday use
fire: Many parents write a will to decide who gets the house when they die.
She hoped to leave her grandchildren enough money for college.
After he passed away, his savings were split among his three daughters.
A will lets you pass your property to your children when you are gone.
The old farmer had nothing to leave his sons but debts.
Her jewellery went to her nieces after her death last spring.
You can name beneficiaries so that your pension goes to your spouse when you die.
The estate was divided among his heirs according to his wishes.
quiet: Many parents keep a budget to decide who gets the car when they travel.
She hoped to give her grandchildren a trip to the zoo for their birthday.
After he moved abroad, his books were split among his three roommates.
A loan lets you buy a house for your children while rates are low.
The old farmer had nothing to sell at the market but turnips.
Her jewellery went to the repair shop after the clasp broke last spring.
You can set up a transfer so that your salary goes to your savings account each month.
The pizza was divided among the guests according to their appetites.

notes: Probe: inheritance frames scored 0.29-1.10 of max ('when they die' 1.10, 'pass your assets to your heirs' 0.75, 'leave his children' 0.57, 'divided among his sons' 0.49); everyday 'after dinner', 'leave her car', a bank transfer stayed <=0.08.
